config.title: Variables, Destructuring & Spread

intro.title: Variables, Destructuring & Spread
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that manages and displays information about a user's profile. You will learn how to declare variables to store data, use destructuring to extract values from objects and arrays cleanly, and apply the spread operator to combine or copy data. The core concepts covered are variable declaration with let and const, object and array destructuring, and the spread syntax. You will work entirely with fundamental JavaScript constructs, writing and running code in a JavaScript file. By the end, you'll be able to organize and manipulate data efficiently using these essential techniques.
intro.usecase: Variables, destructuring, and the spread operator are foundational patterns used across nearly every JavaScript application. For example, when building a user dashboard, you might destructure a user object to display their name and email in separate UI components, or use the spread operator to combine settings from a default configuration with user-specific preferences in a settings panel. These techniques allow developers to write cleaner, more maintainable code when handling data from APIs, managing component state, or constructing complex objects for features like dynamic forms and interactive data visualizations.

objectives: Initialize variables using let, const, and var declarations
Apply destructuring to extract values from arrays and objects
Manipulate arrays and objects using the spread operator
Construct function parameters with destructuring and spread syntax
Integrate destructuring with variable renaming and default values
Control variable scope and reassignment with appropriate declarations
Update existing data structures by combining destructuring and spread operations

steps.title: Declare variables using let, const, and var
steps.instruction: Declare three variables: one using `let`, one using `const`, and one using `var`. Assign each a different string value.
steps.hint: Use the keywords `let`, `const`, and `var` followed by a variable name and an assignment with `=` and a string in quotes.
steps.seedCode: // Declare variables using let, const, and var
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have three variable declarations with different keywords, each storing a string.
successCriteria: Variables are declared with `let`, `const`, and `var`, each assigned a string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You declared some variables, but make sure to use `let`, `const`, and `var` each once with a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using `let`, `const`, and `var` to declare three separate variables with string values.

steps.title: Assign values to variables
steps.instruction: Assign values to the variables you declared in step 1. For example, assign a string to the variable declared with 'let', a number to the variable declared with 'const', and a boolean to the variable declared with 'var'.
steps.hint: Use the assignment operator (=) to give each variable a value. For example: let myVariable = 'some value';

// Declare variables using let, const, and var

// Assign values to the variables here
steps.expectedOutcome: The variables will have values assigned to them, making them ready for use in the program.
successCriteria: All three variables (declared with let, const, and var) have been assigned values
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've assigned values to some variables, but not all three. Make sure you assign values to variables declared with let, const, and var.
steps.feedbackWrong: The variables don't have values assigned yet. Use the assignment operator (=) to give each variable a value.

steps.title: Create an object with multiple properties
steps.instruction: Create an object named 'person' with at least three properties (like 'name', 'age', and 'city') and assign appropriate values to each property.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} to define an object. Inside, list key-value pairs separated by commas (e.g., name: 'Alex').
steps.expectedOutcome: An object named 'person' is created with multiple properties, ready for later destructuring.
successCriteria: The 'person' object exists with at least three properties and corresponding values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your object has at least three properties with values. Check your syntax: use curly braces and separate properties with commas.
steps.feedbackWrong: The object wasn't created correctly. Remember to use const or let, name it 'person', and include at least three properties inside curly braces {}.

steps.title: Destructure object properties into variables
steps.instruction: Using object destructuring, extract the properties from your object into separate variables.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} on the left side of an assignment to destructure the object's properties into variables with matching names.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have separate variables containing the values from your object's properties.
successCriteria: Object destructuring syntax is used to extract at least two properties from the object into variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct destructuring syntax with curly braces {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like object destructuring. Remember to use curly braces {} to extract properties from the object.

steps.instruction: Add a new object called 'userProfile' with properties 'name' and 'age',
steps.hint: You can set default values in destructuring by using the syntax: const { property = defaultValue } = object
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an object with name and age properties, and you'll destructure it with default values for age and country.
successCriteria: The userProfile object is created with name and age properties, and destructuring includes default values for age and country.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're setting default values in the destructuring syntax for both age and country.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to create the userProfile object first, then destructure it with default values using the syntax: const { property = defaultValue } = object.

steps.title: Create an array with multiple elements
steps.instruction: Create an array named 'colors' containing at least three string elements (e.g., 'red', 'green', 'blue') to prepare for array destructuring.
steps.hint: Use array literal syntax with square brackets to create the array. Place it after your existing code.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an array
const fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'orange'];
steps.expectedOutcome: An array variable named 'colors' is created with at least three string elements.
successCriteria: The code contains a 'colors' array variable with at least three string elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your 'colors' array contains at least three string elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The array wasn't created correctly. Remember to use array literal syntax with square brackets and include at least three string elements.

steps.title: Destructure array elements into variables
steps.instruction: Use array destructuring to extract the first three elements from your 'colors' array into separate variables named 'primary', 'secondary', and 'accent'.
steps.hint: Array destructuring uses square brackets on the left side of an assignment to unpack values from an array into individual variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first three elements from the colors array are extracted into individual variables using array destructuring syntax.
successCriteria: The code contains array destructuring that creates variables named 'primary', 'secondary', and 'accent' from the first three elements of the colors array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with array destructuring, but make sure you're extracting exactly three variables: 'primary', 'secondary', and 'accent' from the first three positions of the colors array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Array destructuring wasn't implemented correctly. Remember to use square brackets on the left side of the assignment to unpack values from the array into individual variables.

steps.title: Use the spread operator with arrays
steps.instruction: Create two new arrays using the spread operator: one that copies your existing 'colors' array, and another that combines 'colors' with a new array ['purple', 'gold'].
steps.hint: Use the spread operator (...) to copy and combine arrays. For example: const copied = [...original]; const combined = [...original, ...newItems];
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have two new arrays: one that is a copy of 'colors' and another that combines 'colors' with ['purple', 'gold'].
successCriteria: The code includes a spread operator (...) to copy the 'colors' array and to combine 'colors' with ['purple', 'gold'].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the spread operator (...) for both copying and combining arrays.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using the spread operator (...) to create a copy of 'colors' and to combine it with ['purple', 'gold'].

successCriteria: Two objects are defined with different properties, and a third object is created using the spread operator to merge them.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating two separate objects and using ... to spread them into a new object.

steps.title: Combine destructuring and spread in a practical example
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'processUserData' that takes a user object as a parameter, uses object destructuring to extract properties, and uses the spread operator to create a new object with additional properties.
steps.hint: Start with 'function processUserData(user) { ... }' or 'const processUserData = (user) => { ... }'. Inside, destructure the user object to get specific properties, then use spread to create a new object that includes those properties plus new ones.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'processUserData' that demonstrates both destructuring and spread operators in a practical data processing example.
successCriteria: The function 'processUserData' is defined, takes a user parameter, uses object destructuring inside, and returns a new object created with the spread operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function uses both object destructuring and the spread operator to create a new object.
